record.context_brief: Finite complete indicator systems for conjugacy
record.original_question: For the topological conjugacy classification of quadratic stochastic operators, determine whether there exists a finite complete system of indicator polynomials in the heredity coefficients P_{ij,k}. If such a system exists, find a basis, where an indicator is a polynomial constrained by topological conjugacy and a complete system is one whose bounds imply that two QSOs are topologically conjugate.

Problem 22. Does there exist a finite complete system of indicators? Find the basis of the system of indicators.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{m-1}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^m_{\ge 0}:\sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ denote the $(m-1)$-dimensional simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) on $S^{m-1}$ is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ defined by
\[ (Vx)_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j, \qquad k=1,\dots,m, \]
where the heredity coefficients $P_{ij,k}$ satisfy
\[ P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k}\ge 0,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k}=1 \quad\text{for all } i,j. \]
Two QSOs $V_1,V_2:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ are called topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ with $h\circ V_1 = V_2\circ h$.

A polynomial $f$ in the variables $\{P_{ij,k}\}$ is called an indicator if there exist constants $a_f<b_f$ (depending only on $f$) such that whenever two QSOs $V_1,V_2$ with coefficient arrays $P^{(1)},P^{(2)}$ are topologically conjugate, the values $f(P^{(1)})$ and $f(P^{(2)})$ both lie in the interval $[a_f,b_f]$ (so that $f$ is constrained by topological conjugacy in this sense). A finite collection $f_1,\dots,f_t$ of indicators is called a complete system if, conversely, whenever two QSOs $V_1,V_2$ have all values $f_s(P^{(1)}), f_s(P^{(2)})$ ($s=1,\dots,t$) in their respective indicator intervals, then $V_1$ and $V_2$ are topologically conjugate. A minimal complete system is called a basis.

Question: Does there exist a finite complete system of indicators for the topological-conjugacy classification of quadratic stochastic operators on $S^{m-1}$? If so, exhibit a basis.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was found. The problem is posed as an open problem in the survey on quadratic stochastic operators, and subsequent literature on QSOs (and on topological conjugacy classification of related operators, e.g. arXiv:2505.00577 on diagonal operators) does not appear to provide a finite complete system of indicators or a basis for the QSO conjugacy classification.
